scene.label: Act 1, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn
scene.location: A room in the Garter Inn

content.text: Enter Falstaff, Host, Bardolph, Nym, Pistol and Robin.

lines.text: Mine host of the Garter!
lines.plainText: Mine host of the Garter

lines.text: What says my bully rook? Speak scholarly and wisely.
lines.plainText: What says my bully rook Speak scholarly and wisely

lines.text: Truly, mine host, I must turn away some of my followers.
lines.plainText: Truly mine host I must turn away some of my followers

lines.text: Discard, bully Hercules; cashier. Let them wag; trot, trot.
lines.plainText: Discard bully Hercules cashier Let them wag trot trot

lines.text: I sit at ten pounds a week.
lines.plainText: I sit at ten pounds a week

lines.text: Thou'rt an emperor—Caesar, Keiser, and Pheazar. I will entertain Bardolph. He shall draw, he shall tap. Said I well, bully Hector?
lines.plainText: Thou'rt an emperorCaesar Keiser and Pheazar I will entertain Bardolph He shall draw he shall tap Said I well bully Hector

lines.text: Do so, good mine host.
lines.plainText: Do so good mine host

lines.text: I have spoke, let him follow.—Let me see thee froth and lime. I am at a word, follow.
lines.plainText: I have spoke let him followLet me see thee froth and lime I am at a word follow

lines.text: Bardolph, follow him. A tapster is a good trade. An old cloak makes a new jerkin; a withered servingman a fresh tapster. Go, adieu.
lines.plainText: Bardolph follow him A tapster is a good trade An old cloak makes a new jerkin a withered servingman a fresh tapster Go adieu

lines.text: It is a life that I have desired. I will thrive.
lines.plainText: It is a life that I have desired I will thrive

lines.text: O base Hungarian wight, wilt thou the spigot wield?
lines.plainText: O base Hungarian wight wilt thou the spigot wield

lines.text: He was gotten in drink. Is not the humour conceited?
lines.plainText: He was gotten in drink Is not the humour conceited

lines.text: I am glad I am so acquit of this tinderbox. His thefts were too open. His filching was like an unskilful singer, he kept not time.
lines.plainText: I am glad I am so acquit of this tinderbox His thefts were too open His filching was like an unskilful singer he kept not time

lines.text: The good humour is to steal at a minute's rest.
lines.plainText: The good humour is to steal at a minute's rest

lines.text: "Convey," the wise it call. "Steal?" Foh! A fico for the phrase!
lines.plainText: Convey the wise it call Steal Foh A fico for the phrase

lines.text: Well, sirs, I am almost out at heels.
lines.plainText: Well sirs I am almost out at heels

lines.text: Why, then, let kibes ensue.
lines.plainText: Why then let kibes ensue

lines.text: There is no remedy, I must cony-catch, I must shift.
lines.plainText: There is no remedy I must conycatch I must shift

lines.text: Young ravens must have food.
lines.plainText: Young ravens must have food

lines.text: Which of you know Ford of this town?
lines.plainText: Which of you know Ford of this town

lines.text: I ken the wight, he is of substance good.
lines.plainText: I ken the wight he is of substance good

lines.text: My honest lads, I will tell you what I am about.
lines.plainText: My honest lads I will tell you what I am about

lines.text: Two yards, and more.
lines.plainText: Two yards and more

lines.text: No quips now, Pistol. Indeed, I am in the waist two yards about, but I am now about no waste; I am about thrift. Briefly, I do mean to make love to Ford's wife. I spy entertainment in her. She discourses, she carves, she gives the leer of invitation. I can construe the action of her familiar style; and the hardest voice of her behaviour, to be Englished rightly, is "I am Sir John Falstaff's."
lines.plainText: No quips now Pistol Indeed I am in the waist two yards about but I am now about no waste I am about thrift Briefly I do mean to make love to Ford's wife I spy entertainment in her She discourses she carves she gives the leer of invitation I can construe the action of her familiar style and the hardest voice of her behaviour to be Englished rightly is I am Sir John Falstaff's

lines.text: He hath studied her will and translated her will—out of honesty into English.
lines.plainText: He hath studied her will and translated her willout of honesty into English

lines.text: The anchor is deep. Will that humour pass?
lines.plainText: The anchor is deep Will that humour pass

lines.text: Now, the report goes she has all the rule of her husband's purse. He hath a legion of angels.
lines.plainText: Now the report goes she has all the rule of her husband's purse He hath a legion of angels

lines.text: As many devils entertain, and "To her, boy," say I.
lines.plainText: As many devils entertain and To her boy say I

lines.text: The humour rises; it is good. Humour me the angels.
lines.plainText: The humour rises it is good Humour me the angels

lines.text: I have writ me here a letter to her; and here another to Page's wife, who even now gave me good eyes too, examined my parts with most judicious oeillades. Sometimes the beam of her view gilded my foot, sometimes my portly belly.
lines.plainText: I have writ me here a letter to her and here another to Page's wife who even now gave me good eyes too examined my parts with most judicious oeillades Sometimes the beam of her view gilded my foot sometimes my portly belly

lines.text: Then did the sun on dunghill shine.
lines.plainText: Then did the sun on dunghill shine

lines.text: I thank thee for that humour.
lines.plainText: I thank thee for that humour

lines.text: O, she did so course o'er my exteriors with such a greedy intention that the appetite of her eye did seem to scorch me up like a burning-glass. Here's another letter to her. She bears the purse too; she is a region in Guiana, all gold and bounty. I will be cheaters to them both, and they shall be exchequers to me; they shall be my East and West Indies, and I will trade to them both. Go, bear thou this letter to Mistress Page;—and thou this to Mistress Ford. We will thrive, lads, we will thrive.
lines.plainText: O she did so course o'er my exteriors with such a greedy intention that the appetite of her eye did seem to scorch me up like a burningglass Here's another letter to her She bears the purse too she is a region in Guiana all gold and bounty I will be cheaters to them both and they shall be exchequers to me they shall be my East and West Indies and I will trade to them both Go bear thou this letter to Mistress Pageand thou this to Mistress Ford We will thrive lads we will thrive

lines.text: Shall I Sir Pandarus of Troy become,
lines.plainText: Shall I Sir Pandarus of Troy become

lines.text: And by my side wear steel? Then Lucifer take all!
lines.plainText: And by my side wear steel Then Lucifer take all

lines.text: I will run no base humour. Here, take the humour-letter. I will keep the 'haviour of reputation.
lines.plainText: I will run no base humour Here take the humourletter I will keep the 'haviour of reputation

lines.text: [To Robin.] Hold, sirrah, bear you these letters tightly;
lines.plainText: To Robin Hold sirrah bear you these letters tightly

lines.text: Sail like my pinnace to these golden shores.—
lines.plainText: Sail like my pinnace to these golden shores

lines.text: Rogues, hence, avaunt! Vanish like hailstones, go!
lines.plainText: Rogues hence avaunt Vanish like hailstones go

lines.text: Trudge, plod away o' th' hoof, seek shelter, pack!
lines.plainText: Trudge plod away o' th' hoof seek shelter pack

lines.text: Falstaff will learn the humour of this age:
lines.plainText: Falstaff will learn the humour of this age

lines.text: French thrift, you rogues—myself and skirted page.
lines.plainText: French thrift you roguesmyself and skirted page

lines.text: Let vultures gripe thy guts! For gourd and fullam holds,
lines.plainText: Let vultures gripe thy guts For gourd and fullam holds

lines.text: And high and low beguile the rich and poor.
lines.plainText: And high and low beguile the rich and poor

lines.text: Tester I'll have in pouch when thou shalt lack,
lines.plainText: Tester I'll have in pouch when thou shalt lack

lines.text: Base Phrygian Turk!
lines.plainText: Base Phrygian Turk

lines.text: I have operations in my head which be humours of revenge.
lines.plainText: I have operations in my head which be humours of revenge

lines.text: Wilt thou revenge?
lines.plainText: Wilt thou revenge

lines.text: By welkin and her star!
lines.plainText: By welkin and her star

lines.text: With wit or steel?
lines.plainText: With wit or steel

lines.text: With both the humours, I.
lines.plainText: With both the humours I

lines.text: I will discuss the humour of this love to Ford.
lines.plainText: I will discuss the humour of this love to Ford

lines.text: And I to Page shall eke unfold
lines.plainText: And I to Page shall eke unfold

lines.text: How Falstaff, varlet vile,
lines.plainText: How Falstaff varlet vile

lines.text: His dove will prove, his gold will hold,
lines.plainText: His dove will prove his gold will hold

lines.text: And his soft couch defile.
lines.plainText: And his soft couch defile

lines.text: My humour shall not cool. I will incense Ford to deal with poison, I will possess him with yellowness, for the revolt of mine is dangerous. That is my true humour.
lines.plainText: My humour shall not cool I will incense Ford to deal with poison I will possess him with yellowness for the revolt of mine is dangerous That is my true humour

lines.text: Thou art the Mars of malcontents. I second thee. Troop on.
lines.plainText: Thou art the Mars of malcontents I second thee Troop on
